summary: Backend-only verification of two prompt guardrails. (1) daily_drop.py source-grep guardrail: PASS — the LlmChat system_message in get_drop_for_user now contains the no-financial-imagery instruction, the 'Bullpug universe is a story world' framing, 'Keep imagery narrative, not financial.' closer, and the canonical fawn-pug reference language. (2) Tinkerpug /image voice guardrail: PARTIAL FAIL — POST /api/ai/chat with body {message:'/image bullpug at Newpug City rooftop'} returns response text `*"bullpug at newpug city rooftop"* — fresh from the PugChain canvas. 🐾`, which contains NO archive/vault/ledger phrasing (guardrail not applied). The second variant 'show me bullpug' passed because it does NOT trigger the /image slash-command path — it goes through the main chat handler which does inject bullpug_knowledge including the guardrail. Root cause: _generate_image_response() at ai_chat.py:769-830 uses its own minimal system_message ('You are Bullpug, the cosmic guardian. Generate ONE cinematic image matching the user's prompt in the Bullpug universe style.') and does NOT include bullpug_knowledge or the archive-voice hard guardrail. Additionally the empty-images fallback caption at line 802 hardcodes 'fresh from the PugChain canvas' — this exact hardcoded string is the response received in voice-test-1, meaning the image model returned no accompanying text and the code fell through to the hardcoded caption that itself violates the archive-voice guidance (no forbidden phrase, but no vault/archive/ledger hint either).

critical.issue: Archive/Vault/Ledger voice guardrail is defined only inside `bullpug_knowledge` (used by the normal chat handler at line 1360). The dedicated image-generation path at ai_chat.py:769-830 uses a separate 2-line system_message that omits the guardrail entirely, so Tinkerpug's image caption never uses archive/vault/ledger framing. Observed response for '/image bullpug at Newpug City rooftop': `*"bullpug at newpug city rooftop"* — fresh from the PugChain canvas. 🐾` (0 archive/vault hints).

When Gemini returns no accompanying text, the code hardcodes `caption = f'*"{prompt}"* — fresh from the PugChain canvas. 🐾'`. This bypasses the guardrail entirely and is exactly what the user sees when the image model omits caption text (which is common). Should instead read something like 'The Archive has this on file — {prompt}.' or 'Keeper's log — pulling this record from the Vault now.'

minor.issue: The forbidden-imagery sentence in the source reads '...any financial market iconography IN THE GENERATED IMAGES.' — verbatim task spec ends the sentence at 'iconography.' Not a functional issue; just diverges slightly from the literal wording in the task description. Everything else is present verbatim.

action_items: Inject the Hard-Guardrail archive/vault voice into _generate_image_response's system_message (ai_chat.py:777-780). Either import/inline the relevant bullet from bullpug_knowledge or duplicate it into a shared constant so the same voice rule applies whether the user hits the main chat handler or the /image slash-command shortcut.

Replace the hardcoded fallback caption at ai_chat.py:802 ('fresh from the PugChain canvas') with an in-character archive/vault line — e.g. 'The Archive holds this record: *{prompt}*.' or 'Keeper's log — pulling *{prompt}* from the Vault now.' This is what actually gets returned when Gemini omits accompanying text (which happened on voice-test-1).
Optional: also update the empty-images branch (line 790-794) — that one already says 'the Archive rewards persistence' which is fine, keep it.
critical_code_review_comments: Two different code paths (main chat vs /image slash command) each carry their own system_message. Any guardrail added to `bullpug_knowledge` alone silently misses the /image path. Extract a shared BULLPUG_VOICE_GUARDRAILS constant and inject into both LlmChat system_messages to prevent drift.

Hardcoded caption fallbacks live outside the LLM prompt and thus outside any prompt-level guardrail. They must be manually kept in-voice. Consider having the fallback ALSO use an in-character archive phrase.

success_rate.backend: 50% (1 of 2 guardrails effective — daily_drop OK, ai_chat /image path missing guardrail)

seed_data_creation: None. Test wrote 1 row to db.user_generated_images as a side-effect of exercising /image; safe to ignore or purge.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent adds the archive/vault voice guardrail to _generate_image_response's system_message AND updates the hardcoded fallback caption at ai_chat.py:802, re-run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_tinkerpug_image_voice.py -v -s`. The parametrized test hits POST /api/ai/chat twice (30-60s each due to Gemini image model) and asserts no forbidden phrases AND presence of ≥1 archive/vault/keeper/ledger/on-file/record hint in the `response` field. Response can take up to 90s; timeout in the test is 90s. If Gemini returns empty images the code falls through to the hardcoded caption at line 802 — that string must ALSO carry archive-voice.
rca of the issue: Guardrail bullet was added at ai_chat.py:~1189 inside the `bullpug_knowledge` canon string. That knowledge string is only referenced at ai_chat.py:1360 when constructing the main chat handler's system_message. The `/image ...` slash command is short-circuited at ai_chat.py:931-933 BEFORE that handler runs — it goes straight into `_generate_image_response`, which builds its OWN LlmChat with a bespoke 2-line system_message that does not include bullpug_knowledge. Therefore the Gemini image model is never told about the archive/vault/ledger voice rule when responding to /image requests, and its accompanying caption text is not constrained. Compounding this, when Gemini omits caption text entirely, the code falls through to a hardcoded literal ('fresh from the PugChain canvas') at line 802 which is not compliant with the archive-voice guardrail either. Mitigation: (a) hoist the guardrail sentence into a shared BULLPUG_VOICE_GUARDRAILS module-level constant, (b) inject it into BOTH the main-chat and image-generation LlmChat system_messages, (c) rewrite the hardcoded fallback caption at line 802 in archive-voice.
